title: Minimal smooth envelopes and etale comparisons
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme of finite type over a characteristic-zero field $k$ and $x\in X$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. A minimal smooth envelope at $x$ means a local closed embedding $X\hookrightarrow M$ into a smooth $k$-scheme for which the induced map
$$\Omega_{M/k}\otimes\kappa(x)\longrightarrow\Omega_{X/k}\otimes\kappa(x)$$
is an isomorphism; $\Omega$ denotes the module generated by symbols $da$ with additivity, the Leibniz rule, and $dc=0$ for $c\in k$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Such envelopes exist after restriction and etale localization. Any smooth local envelope contains a minimal smooth closed envelope through $X$. Given two minimal envelopes of the same scheme germ, there is a common etale neighbourhood of the pointed closed pairs, identifying the induced neighbourhoods of $X$ by their given identification. Equivalently their henselian ambient germs are isomorphic by an isomorphism inducing the given quotient isomorphism. A smooth closed pair $N\hookrightarrow M$ admits, etale-locally along $N$, a retraction onto an etale neighbourhood of $N$ and transverse regular parameters: locally the pair is the zero section in an etale neighbourhood of $N\times\mathbf A^r$. These comparisons allow adjoining and eliminating transverse regular parameters and respect pullback of specified ideal sheaves on $X$.

proof.text: An affine finite-type presentation embeds a neighbourhood of $x$ in affine space, which is smooth. Apply the conormal-kernel coordinate slice to this or any supplied smooth envelope. Its $M_0$ contains $X$ and has differential fibre $V/K$, canonically the differential fibre of $X$ by the kernel definition. Thus it is minimal; this proves existence and the inside-envelope assertion.

proof.text: For two minimal envelopes, identify their $X$ germs. The compatible-coordinate lifting lemma supplies etale maps $e_a$ agreeing on $X$. Apply the two-etale case of the fibre-product refinement: the two inverse images of $X$ are the same specified copy, with marked residue field unchanged. These are the required common pointed closed pairs.

source.place: Assembly of the retained coordinate route; old Steps [4, 5], as exposed by the cited statements.

proof.text: Apply the pointed-etale henselization isomorphism to each projection at the marked point. Its quotient compatibility identifies both closed quotients with the henselization of $X$ and preserves its given identification. Compose one ambient isomorphism with the other's inverse. This gives the henselian existence formulation; the common etale neighbourhood was already constructed, so no algebraization of a prescribed isomorphism is needed.

source.place: Assembly of the retained coordinate route; old Steps [6], as exposed by the cited statements.

proof.text: For a smooth closed pair $N\hookrightarrow M$ and $y\in N$, the smooth-pair local coordinates give an etale $h=(g,f):U\to\mathbf A^{d+r}_k$ with $N\cap U=h^{-1}(\mathbf A^d\times0)$ and $e_N=g|_{N\cap U}$ etale. Shrink $U$ to an affine $W\ni y$; open restriction keeps $h$ etale. Apply the one-etale refinement to $W\times_{\mathbf A^d}(N\cap W)$ using $g,e_N$. It gives an etale ambient neighbourhood $P$ with $p^{-1}N=s(N)$ and a retraction $q:P\to N$. The map $(q,f):P\to N\times\mathbf A^r$ is the restriction of the base change of $h$, hence etale. Thus $q$ is smooth of relative dimension $r$, by affine-space smoothness and relative-dimension composition.

proof.text: The centred smooth-section chart theorem applies to $q$ and its closed section. It supplies affine $T,U$, the Cartesian zero section, actual regular coordinate parameters generating the section ideal, and the augmentation quotient $\Gamma(T)$. Compose the etale ambient maps. Apply this also to $M_0\hookrightarrow M$ from Step 1: it adjoins or eliminates transverse parameters. Empty parameter lists give the same conclusions for $r=0$.

source.place: Assembly of the retained coordinate route; old Steps [9], as exposed by the cited statements.

proof.text: For ideals use affine quotients. If $B\twoheadrightarrow A=B/I$ and $B\to C$ has $C/IC=A$, then $\pi^{-1}J$ is generated by $I$ and lifts of elements of $J$; extension to $C$ is exactly the inverse image of $J$. In a transverse chart quotient by its parameters gives the same formula. These equalities on affine restrictions prove the specified ideal-sheaf compatibility.
